html:
The bushfire season of 2019 and 2020 in Australia, known as the Black Summer, one of the most destructive fire seasons ever recorded anywhere.

2019 was the hottest and driest year on record in Australia. Fires started early, in winter, and by December huge blazes were burning across New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia. Estimates of the area burned range from about 18 to over 24 million hectares, depending on what is counted, an area larger than many countries.

Thirty-three people died in the fires and thousands of homes were destroyed. At Mallacoota thousands of people were trapped on the beach and evacuated by navy ships. Smoke choked Sydney and Canberra for weeks. A study estimated that about three billion animals were killed or displaced, and much of Kangaroo Island burned.

Prime Minister Scott Morrison was criticised for taking a holiday in Hawaii as the crisis grew. A royal commission later urged better national planning for disasters. Scientists linked the extreme heat and drought to climate change, which made the fires a turning point in Australian politics.
sum: The bushfire season of 2019 and 2020 in Australia, known as the Black Summer, one of the most destructive fire seasons ever recorded anywhere.
